premise.claim: KEP-531's description of main's renderer is accurate: leaderWorkerPattern injects profiles into the leader template only; customComponentsPattern injects into every declared component; injectContainers is inert; the legacy containers merge is env/args-only and no-ops for init containers; env injectors run after the sidecar stage, dedupe last-wins, and cover profile-injected containers.
premise.evidence: 16/16 harness tests pass on the PR head tree (code identical to base); see results/unit-discovery.json and results/unit-structure.json. One KEP sentence is contradicted: Compatibility #6's 'matching the v1alpha2 cap' — no MaxItems exists on either API version (S3).

_docFindings._note: The debate findings F1..Fn are defects in the KEP TEXT. re-verify.sh judges the code-fact claims above; a KEP text revision does not change test outcomes — doc fixes are judged by re-reading keps/531-engine-runtime-profile-injection/README.md at the new head. The structural tests (S*) flip red if the underlying code changes, signalling that the KEP text must be re-checked rather than that it was fixed.

F1.summary: KEP Compatibility #6 claims v1alpha2 already caps roles at MaxItems=16; no cap exists on either version, and the planned tightening breaks stored-object updates in both versions, not just v1alpha1.

F2.summary: kep.yaml claims the KEP answers issue #531's inventory 'point by point' including unconsumed updateStrategy; the README never mentions updateStrategy or profile-change propagation.

F3.summary: component field DNS-label pattern vs unconstrained InstanceComponent.Name.

F4.summary: KEP cites kubelet last-wins for duplicate mountPath; apiserver actually rejects with 'must be unique'.
